extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, IP attorneys, applicants, and examiners working with Chinese (CNIPA) patent applications
extracted.subtask_description: Summarises CNIPA's amended Patent Examination Guidelines (effective 1 Jan 2026) setting substantive examination standards for AI/algorithm/data inventions, BitTorrent/video-coding, plant varieties/biological breeding, inventiveness assessment, dual filings, invalidation procedure and inventor eligibility in China.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject-matter: algorithm/business-methods violating law or social ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: Invention patent applications containing algorithm or business method features should not be granted patent rights, provided that the data collection, tag management, rule setting or recommended decision making contains any content that violates laws or social ethics or harms public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: an application using facial recognition data collected in public areas for precise in-mall marketing would be ineligible because China’s Personal Information Protection Law limits such data usage without consent. Another example: an emergency decision-making model for autonomous vehicles that uses pedestrians’ gender and age to decide whom to protect would be rejected for undermining equal right to life, reinforcing bias, and harming public trust. The rule embeds legality and ethics/public-interest considerations into subject-matter eligibility for AI/data-related inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventiveness for algorithm/data-related inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Algorithmic and technical features must support and interact with each other in terms of functionality for the contribution to inventive step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the invention only involves simple replacement of elements (e.g., collecting data from objects completely different from the prior art) without adjustments or improvements to deep learning, model construction or training processes, it will be deemed non-inventive. Examiner focus: functional interaction between algorithmic and technical features — mere change of data source or trivial substitutions do not establish inventive step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient disclosure for AI model building and training
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent descriptions relating to technical solutions for building or training AI models must clearly depict the modules, hierarchies and connection relationships essential for the models, as well as the specific steps and parameters required for training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the invention applies an AI model or algorithm in a specific field or scenario, the description should clearly state how the model/algorithm is combined with that field/scenario and how input and output data are configured to indicate inherent correlation, so a person skilled in the art can implement the solution. Expect requirements for module diagrams, hierarchies, connection relationships, explicit training steps and parameter values.

rubrics_metrics.name: BitTorrent-related subject-matter eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: BitTorrent, if claimed as a standalone subject matter, shall fall under unpatentable rules and methods of intellectual activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, in digital video-coding/decoding fields, if a specific method for generating BitTorrent is claimed as the technical solution, and the method for storing or transmitting and the computer-readable storage medium for storing the said BitTorrent achieve optimized configuration of storage or transmission resources, then such storage/transmission methods and computer-readable storage media are patentable. Key: tie BitTorrent-related claims to technical solutions that optimize resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and exclusion of plants as patent subject-matter
rubrics_metrics.description: A plant is defined as a typically non-moving organism capable of utilising photosynthesis to synthesise carbohydrates and proteins from inorganic substances. Untreated, naturally occurring wild plants found in nature are excluded from patent protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where wild plants are artificially selected or improved and have industrial application value, they are no longer considered mere scientific discoveries. The amendment broadens eligible subject matter in plant-related fields but explicitly excludes untreated wild plants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant variety definition and population requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: "Plant varieties" are redefined as a plant population artificially selected or discovered and improved, with consistent morphological and biological characteristics and relatively stable genetic traits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plants and reproductive materials obtained by artificial breeding or improvement from discovered wild plants shall not be deemed plant varieties if they lack consistent morphological/biological characteristics or relatively stable genetic traits in their population. Examiners will assess consistency and stability at population level when determining eligibility as a plant variety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility of genetically modified plants
rubrics_metrics.description: A genetically modified plant produced through recombinant DNA genetic engineering — if it still falls under the category of 'plant varieties' — remains ineligible subject matter for plant-variety patenting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such new genetically modified plants should instead be protected under the Regulations on the Protection of New Plant Varieties in China. The guideline separates patent eligibility from plant variety protection for GM plants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of inventiveness: whole-claim assessment and non-contributing features
rubrics_metrics.description: The claimed technical solution should be subject to the inventiveness assessment test in its entirety, rather than a test of inventiveness of certain technical features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In principle, inclusion of features not contributing to solving the technical problems shall have no bearing on inventiveness assessment. The revision discourages piling excessive, irrelevant features into claims to try to manufacture inventive step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual filing of invention and utility model patents: only one patent granted
rubrics_metrics.description: Only one patent can be granted for dual filings of the same invention as an invention patent and a utility model; once an invention patent application is granted, the applicant must abandon the utility model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Previously permissible parallel filings to secure varying scopes are disallowed going forward. During filing, the applicant is obligated to declare the concurrent invention and utility model patent applications. Practical effect: applicants cannot use simultaneous filings to obtain two patents for the same subject‑matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidation petitioner eligibility: exclusion of patent agencies/attorneys
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent agencies or attorneys are disqualified from acting as an invalidation petitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offenders face fines, temporary suspension of new patent businesses and potential licence revocation. The change aims to curb third‑party or proxy-driven invalidation actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal of invalidation requests that do not reflect petitioner's true intentions
rubrics_metrics.description: An invalidation request that fails to reflect the petitioner’s true intentions shall be dismissed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule targets illegal or malicious invalidation actions using 'straw men' to initiate proceedings. Implementation details remain to be seen, but examiners/boards will assess whether petitions genuinely reflect the petitioner's purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of non bis in idem to repeated invalidation actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Non bis in idem principle is applied to curtail repeated invalidation actions based on grounds and/or evidence not only identical but also substantially identical with those submitted in prior invalidation proceedings in which CNIPA has already made an invalidation decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests reusing identical or substantially identical grounds/evidence to relitigate the same issues may be barred. The aim is to prevent repeated attacks on the same patent using the same material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor eligibility and verification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are required to fill in the authentic inventors and the identity information of all inventors; an inventor must be a natural person, explicitly banning listing any entity, group or AI independently or therein as inventors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent agencies are tasked to verify the applicant's identity and contact information in the request form. This enforces authenticity of inventor designation and forbids listing non‑natural persons (e.g., AI) as inventors.
